requirements.value:
- Install or update Engram could leave the old plugin in place on a Vita that wouldn't let the file be renamed over or removed. It now writes over the file where it is when that happens, and a copy that still fails shows the system's error code and puts the old plugin back. If you installed engram_installer.vpk while 1.6 was a pre-release and Settings still says Engram 1.5, install this one and choose Install or update Engram again.
- Fonts > Apps sets itself up: giving an app a font adds Engram's line under that app in taiHEN's config.txt, and setting it back to System Font takes it out. Engram keeps a copy from before each change (config.txt.engram-old) and the original (ur0:data/engram/tai_config_original.txt).
- My other projects, in the installer: the author's other plugins and apps for the Vita, with photos, each release's notes, and an Install button for the newest.
- Other plugins' Settings entries could disappear next to Engram's (Turbo Storage's, for one). Engram now adds its rows after theirs when its line comes straight after henkaku.suprx (see [Install](#install)), and adds a smaller page otherwise, so Turbo Storage's still fits.
- Put your fonts in ur0:data/engram/fonts (.ttf, .otf or .pvf, up to 40). Every list in Fonts shows the fonts it finds there, by file name.
- Install or update Engram copies the plugin to ur0:tai and adds its lines to taiHEN's config.txt (steps 1 and 2 of [Install](#install)), keeping a copy of the config from before.
- My other projects shows the author's other plugins and apps for the Vita, each with photos and what it does. Download lists a project's releases with their notes, and installs the newest one through the Vita's own installer; an older release can be read about and opened on GitHub. A plugin's install is its own installer app, which then puts the plugin in and keeps it up to date. Everything downloaded is checked against the SHA-256 GitHub lists for it.
- Copy engram.suprx to ur0:tai/engram.suprx.
- For Fonts, put your fonts in ur0:data/engram/fonts. Engram makes the folder the first time it runs.
- Another plugin's Settings entry disappeared (Turbo Storage's, say): put Engram's line straight after henkaku.suprx under NPXS10015 and NPXS10016, as in [Install](#install).
- config.txt looks wrong after a font change: the copy from before the change is config.txt.engram-old beside it, and the one from before Engram ever changed it is ur0:data/engram/tai_config_original.txt. Copy either back over config.txt with VitaShell, then reboot.

requirements.value:
- No boot plugin changes: just install the VPK.
- Install VitaRecovery_v1.2.3.vpk with VitaShell. No boot plugin changes, so you do not need to reinstall Boot Recovery. "Enable Unsafe Homebrew" must stay ticked in HENkaku Settings.
- You have a basic understanding of PS Vita custom firmware and the risks involved in modifying system files.
- Boot Recovery: installer for the boot plugins (Install / Update / Uninstall)
- Safe Mode, Undo Safe Mode (puts back your exact config from before Safe Mode), View & Toggle, Re-enable All (turns on every plugin), Reset to Minimal (old config kept as config.txt.before_reset), Backup / Restore config.
- Back Up Layout: copies ur0:shell/db/app.db to ux0:data/vita_recovery/layout/app.db and checks the copy before it replaces the old backup. The backup before it is kept too ("Older"). Nothing is rotated if the layout hasn't changed.
- Restore Latest Backup / Restore Older Backup: builds the restored layout on a copy (the live database is never edited), shows what will happen, then restarts the Vita. Early in the next boot the boot plugin swaps it in and keeps the replaced database as ur0:shell/db/app.db.prelayout. - Recommended (VPK only): Download LinuxOnVita.vpk, install it via VitaShell, and launch LinuxOnVita to automatically deploy ux0:/linux/ and boot Linux.
- Custom Firmware: Any PS Vita (1000 OLED, 2000 Slim, or PlayStation TV) running 3.60 or 3.65 with HENkaku / Ensō (see vita.hacks.guide (https://vita.hacks.guide)).
- Open Settings -> HENkaku Settings -> check Enable Unsafe Homebrew [✓]. If unchecked, the loader plugin will fail with error 0x8002D003.
- Supported Storage (SD2Vita or Internal eMMC):
- No Sony memory card required! Linux boot files and runtime storage can be installed directly to your SD2Vita (ux0:) or internal system storage (ur0:).
- Note on Sony Memory Cards: The proprietary Sony memory card interface (MSIF) cannot be detected or accessed by Linux at runtime. You do not need an official Sony memory card to install or boot Linux.
- > Kernel Plugin Compatibility - Read Before Installing
- > LinuxOnVita is developed and tested on a PS Vita 1000 (OLED) running 3.65 Ensō with no additional plugins or mods installed. Behaviour on other configurations is not guaranteed.
- > Several users have reported boot loops on return to VitaOS after running Linux when USB streaming, storage remapping, or other kernel-level plugins are active. Known problematic plugins include:
- > - VitaUSBStream (and related streaming plugins)
- > - Any other KERNEL section plugin that hooks USB, storage, or partition remapping
- > These plugins re-initialise hardware at startup. Because the baremetal loader reconfigures the MSIF memory card controller and USB subsystem directly during Linux boot, some plugins can encounter unexpected hardware state on the return reboot and crash.

evidence.text: Recommended (VPK only): Download LinuxOnVita.vpk, install it via VitaShell, and launch LinuxOnVita to automatically deploy ux0:/linux/ and boot Linux.
Custom Firmware: Any PS Vita (1000 OLED, 2000 Slim, or PlayStation TV) running 3.60 or 3.65 with HENkaku / Ensō (see vita.hacks.guide (https://vita.hacks.guide)).
Open Settings -> HENkaku Settings -> check Enable Unsafe Homebrew [✓]. If unchecked, the loader plugin will fail with error 0x8002D003.
Supported Storage (SD2Vita or Internal eMMC):
No Sony memory card required! Linux boot files and runtime storage can be installed directly to your SD2Vita (ux0:) or internal system storage (ur0:).
Note on Sony Memory Cards: The proprietary Sony memory card interface (MSIF) cannot be detected or accessed by Linux at runtime. You do not need an official Sony memory card to install or boot Linux.
> Kernel Plugin Compatibility - Read Before Installing
> LinuxOnVita is developed and tested on a PS Vita 1000 (OLED) running 3.65 Ensō with no additional plugins or mods installed. Behaviour on other configurations is not guaranteed.
> Several users have reported boot loops on return to VitaOS after running Linux when USB streaming, storage remapping, or other kernel-level plugins are active. Known problematic plugins include:
> - VitaUSBStream (and related streaming plugins)
> - Any other KERNEL section plugin that hooks USB, storage, or partition remapping

> These plugins re-initialise hardware at startup. Because the baremetal loader reconfigures the MSIF memory card controller and USB subsystem directly during Linux boot, some plugins can encounter unexpected hardware state on the return reboot and crash.
> 1. Hold the L trigger while powering on to temporarily bypass all taiHEN plugins and boot to the LiveArea.
> 2. Open VitaShell and navigate to ur0:tai/config.txt (or ux0:tai/config.txt).
> 3. Comment out or remove the offending kernel plugin lines (prefix with #).
> If you are running a heavily modded Vita with multiple kernel plugins, consider testing LinuxOnVita on a cleaner setup first.

> Baremetal OS execution bypasses VitaOS storage drivers and low-level power safeguards. If an experimental kernel boot hangs and requires a 30-second hard power-off (holding the Power button), lower-end or budget microSD cards (particularly cards lacking power-loss protection capacitors) can suffer FTL (Flash Translation Layer) controller lockups where the internal controller panics and all sectors return 0xFF.

> LinuxOnVita minimizes storage risk by mounting partitions read-only by default, executing synchronous device-level filesystem flushes (sceIoSync / ksceIoSync) and hardware settling delays prior to Syscon soft-reset, and pre-staging boot files directly in DRAM. However, hardware hangs can happen with early software. Always maintain a full backup of your microSD card image or vital data.
> Storage & SD Card Safety Protection

> LinuxOnVita automatically mounts your SD2Vita (ux0:) and internal eMMC (ur0:) partitions in read-only mode by default. This ensures VitaOS database files and exFAT/FAT volumes are never marked dirty or exposed to write interruptions during reboots or crashes. To temporarily enable write access, run vita-storage rw ux0, and always reboot cleanly using vita-reboot.
In VitaShell, highlight LinuxOnVita.vpk and press CROSS (✕) to install. You can install it to any partition (ux0:, uma0:, etc.) - it does not matter where the app itself lives.

> If you already have an older version of LinuxOnVita installed, transfer and install the latest LinuxOnVita.vpk in VitaShell, launch the app, and press TRIANGLE (△) to reinstall and update the Linux setup (<mount>/linux/). Pressing CROSS (✕) immediately would otherwise boot the older kernel and loaders already on your memory card. To launch Linux with step-by-step diagnostic logging, press SQUARE (□) instead.
Unsafe Homebrew is disabled. On your Vita, go to Settings -> HENkaku Settings -> check Enable Unsafe Homebrew.

requirements.value:
- The <mount> prefix uses the selected Adrenaline storage device (ux0 by default, or mounted uma0). In 02.17, the install dialog shows this destination; installed PSP/PS1 badges can also show the detected device (ux0, uma0, imc0, or xmc0).
- Essential plugins prompt after theme + News: detects missing kubridge, fd_fix (file + config line) and libshacccg (file only); one-tap install + reboot
- Install is append-only to config.txt (never deletes existing lines). After one or more plugin installs the client shows a Restart required modal (soft reset via scePowerRequestColdReset); LiveArea exit is blocked until restart. Hold L at boot to disable taiHEN plugins if something goes wrong.
- If any are missing, a modal offers Install plugins or Remind me later. Install uses the same Plugin pipeline and sequential queue.

- Tidewater is a from-scratch Rust reimplementation of the Warcraft II: Battle.net Edition engine, including Beyond the Dark Portal, that runs on your own copy of the game. You can play both campaigns in single player, start a custom game on any map, and play early LAN multiplayer. Tidewater contains no game data: it reads the files of your own copy.
- Your own copy of the game. Tidewater needs Warcraft II: Battle.net Edition (for example the GOG release, or the Battle.net Edition CD). No game data is included. The 1995 DOS edition is not supported.
- The AppImage is built for the Steam Deck (SteamOS) as well as other desktop Linux systems. On a Steam Deck (SteamOS, Desktop Mode) it starts, imports the game files, and its scripted test scenes draw and sound frame for frame the same as on macOS. Playing it by hand, Game Mode and the Deck's controls are still being tested, so expect rough edges and please report them. It needs glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, SteamOS 3).
- Run it by double-clicking, then [import your game files](#import-your-game-files). Put the file somewhere you can write to (your home folder), as updates replace it.
- Then copy your game files to ux0:data/Tidewater. The Vita app can't play without them. Copy a game folder or a CD image there (VitaShell's FTP or USB), then choose Scan again on the first-run screen.
- main menu. It is hidden when the game files are read in place with --install.

- Start with the [project README](../README.md) to install, import your game files and play. This page indexes the design documents and the behaviour specifications behind the code.
